newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rouble dips on T-bill selling.
newsitem.headline: Rouble dips on T-bill selling.

text.p: The rouble eased in lively trading on Friday as commercial banks sold some government bonds and invested in dollars and overnight rouble credits, dealers said.
"(The T-bill) auctions are over and there are not many other investment opportunities but buying dollars," an Interbank Finance House dealer said.

Neftekhimbank dealer Vladimir Zrazhevsky said the supply of roubles could increase after some major operators sold some government securities to investors and smaller operators without access to auction trading.
On Wednesday the central bank auctioned 7.50 trillion roubles of six-month T-bills and 3.50 trillion roubles of a new tranche of OFZ interest-bearing bonds.

Roubles for today settlement were quoted at 5,377-79 per dollar compared with an early 5,376-79 and 5,370-73 late on Thursday. Tomorrow roubles eased to 5,385-87 per dollar from yesterday's late 5,379-82.
The central bank said it had set 5,350/5,390 as its bid and offer rates against the dollar on Friday.
Overnight rouble credits yielded 15-25 percent compared with Thursday's late 30-50 percent.
